1.explanation: To add Mermaid support you must: 1) Register the new language in components.js under the languages map (so Prism knows about “mermaid” and how to load its grammar). 2) Update the build paths in gulpfile.js/paths.js (add components/prism-mermaid.js to the main components array and, if needed, the autoloader config). 3) Include the new component in the documentation pipeline by modifying jsDoc.files in gulpfile.js/docs.js (within docsCreate) so tutorial pages and API docs include the Mermaid grammar. These files/functions are the exact points where Prism’s language definitions, build process, and documentation are configured, and they all must be updated to fully integrate Mermaid support.
1.bug_scenario: A user is trying to add Mermaid diagram support to Prism. They write a code block in Mermaid syntax (e.g. a flowchart with “graph TD” and nodes like A[Start] → B{Is it?} → …) but Prism neither recognizes nor highlights the Mermaid keywords or renders the diagram. The screenshots show the intended flowchart rendered from Mermaid text, but Prism currently has no Mermaid language definition registered.

2.explanation:
• components.js declares all built-in Prism languages in its languages object. To support Mermaid you must add an entry for ‘mermaid’ there so Prism knows how to recognize and load its grammar.
• gulpfile.js/paths.js’s main array drives which language components are included in a custom prism.js build. You must include 'components/prism-mermaid.js' (or similar) so the build system bundles the Mermaid grammar.
• gulpfile.js/docs.js maintains jsDoc.files—the list of components to include in API/docs generation. You need to add the new prism-mermaid.js file so docsCreate will pick it up and generate reference documentation for Mermaid.
• docsCreate is the function that reads jsDoc.files and pipes them through gulp‐jsdoc3; without updating it Mermaid support won’t appear in the generated docs.
2.bug_scenario: The user wants Prism to support the "mermaid" diagram‐definition language. In the screenshot they’ve embedded a Mermaid flowchart (the familiar Start→Is it?→OK/Rethink→End diagram), but Prism neither highlights nor auto–loads a grammar for "mermaid", so code blocks remain unstyled or errors occur when autoloader tries to fetch an undefined language.
